page.layout: Running head at top; two coin illustrations (no printed text block beside them); one column of main text below, three paragraphs, no margin notes.

main_text.p: ARTEMIVS, qui & Anastasius secundus, ab exercitu Imperator creatus, in Philippicum, uti dictum est, insurrexit, regno oculisque eum priuauit, nec tamen occidit. Hic imperium adeptus est anno mundi 4676. à Christo nato 714. Cum optime quæ ad pietatem attinent instituisset, classem ingentē aduersus Arabes in Alexandriam misit. Verùm classiarij quidam contu-macius agentes, qui illum oderant, domum reuersi, Theodosium ignobilem alioqui virum Imperatorem creant: captaque Con-stantinopoli, monasterio Anastasium includunt, annos tres Im-perantem. Vide Pau. Diac. lib. 8. Egna. lib. 2. Ab. Vrsp.

THEODOSIVS Atramitenus coactus à militibus sum-psit imperium, anno mundi 4679. à Christo nato 717. Hic ad Niceam graui prælio Artemium vicit: obscuro licet loco natus, non pœnitedum Imperatore egisset, si diutius illi per Leonem & Cononem, Orietis præfectos, imperare licuisset. Verùm cùm Leonem exercitus Imperatorem dixisset, pertæsus belli ciuilis Theodosius cessit imperio, monasticam vitam amplexatus. Vide Diac. lib. 8. Egna. lib. 2. Ab Vrsper. hic annum imperat.

LEO Isaurus sceleratus, imperat post Theodosiū. huius tem-poribus Saraceni triénali obsidione terra mariq; Constantinopolim obsident: verùm peste fameque cōfecti, à Bulgaris etiam sæpe victi, classe magna ex parte igne sub aquis ardēte cōsum-pta, numinis iram sensere: nec minori interim clade in urbe sæuitum, trecenta & amplius ciuium millia peste fameque con-sumpta sunt. Hic, in gratia duorum Iudæorum, imagines san-ctorum deiecit atque incendit. imperauit annis 24. Vide Diac. lib. 8. Egna. lib. 2.

page.notes: Two coin woodcuts stand above the text, not transcribed: left, the obverse of Theodosius III and Anastasius II with the legend "THEODOSIVS III IMP ANASTASIVS II AVG" around the rim; right, Leo III with the legend "LEO ISMARVS III IMP" (partly read, the rim letters are worn). The coin legends are part of the illustrations, so they are described here and not in the text. Readings of "Vrsp." and "Vrsper" are assumed from the long-s form, the printed glyph could be "Vrfp" or "Vrfper". "pœnitedum" and "Cum" are copied as they appear. The word "Imperatore" in the Theodosius paragraph is printed as shown.
